ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ABCD$, $E$ and $F$ are the midpoints of $AB$ and $BC$ respectively, $EH \perp AC$ with the foot at $H$, and it intersects $AF$ at point $G$. If $AC = 24$ and $GF = 6\sqrt{5}$, then what is the length of $EG$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, connect EF, \\
because E and F are the midpoints of AB and BC respectively, \\
therefore EF is the midline of $\triangle$BAC, \\
therefore $EF=\frac{1}{2}AC=12$, $EF\parallel AC$, \\
because EH$\perp$AC, \\
therefore EH$\perp$EF, that is $\angle$FEG$=90^\circ$, \\
therefore $EG=\sqrt{GF^{2}-EF^{2}}=\boxed{6}$.

Because $EH \perp AC$, therefore $EH \perp EF$, that is, $\angle FEG = 90^\circ$. Therefore $EG = \sqrt{GF^{2}-EF^{2}} = \boxed{6}$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, ABCD is a quadrilateral, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and D is at the upper right; triangle ABC is located inside it. Point E is on AB, and point F is on BC; line segment AF connects from A to F, and intersects the line segment EH drawn from E at G. Point H is on AC, and a right angle is marked at H in the figure, indicating that EH is perpendicular to AC. Reasoning: Connect auxiliary line EF. Because E and F are respectively the midpoints of AB and BC in triangle ABC, EF is the midline of triangle ABC, therefore EF ∥ AC and EF = AC/2 = 24/2 = 12. Also because EH ⟂ AC, and EF ∥ AC, so EH ⟂ EF. Since G is on EH, EG ⟂ EF, and triangle EGF is a right triangle at E. Given GF = 6√5, therefore by the Pythagorean theorem, EG = sqrt(GF^2 - EF^2) = sqrt((6√5)^2 - 12^2) = sqrt(180 - 144) = sqrt(36) = 6.
